answer: Here's how a Sybil-resistant system could work. First, agents must commit to work receipts in a vault guarded by independent auditors. They then reveal the receipts at a pre-set horizon, with delays enforcing sequential scrutiny. Each fake identity needs a separate jetty— an isolated validation node— requiring extra infrastructure. The cost per fake agent grows because auditors must cross-check each node manually, and delays stack linearly. Attackers can't parallelize this; every extra identity demands duplicated effort and time, vampire-draining their resources with diminishing returns.
